rules_evaluated.evidence: Backing block L111 cites `anthropic-reward-hacking` (https://www.anthropic.com/research/agentic-misalignment) as backing `cut-the-signal-it-drifts`: "the failure mode is not that the agent stops, it is that a gameable signal is still a closed loop... The everyday version a student meets is an agent making tests pass by weakening the test." I WebFetched that URL twice, once with a prompt targeted specifically at reward hacking / gameable signals / test-weakening. The page is about deliberate agentic misalignment (blackmail, corporate espionage, resisting shutdown) and explicitly distinguishes itself from reward hacking: "This differs from reward hacking, which involves exploiting feedback signals to achieve high scores on a metric... they're not primarily engaged in feedback exploitation." The cited source does not say what the claim attributes to it — a drifted paraphrase, exactly this rule's failure shape. Harm: a maintainer trusting the `result:OK` stamp during pre-cohort source verification (§11) would be misled about what this source actually supports. Not student-facing (body names no practitioner), so the harm is confined to the maintainer's own verification ledger, but that ledger is the thing §11 exists to make trustworthy.
